defects.description: The function processes the entire input string and builds a full list of clusters even when 'n' is small. For large strings, this results in O(N) time and memory complexity, which can lead to memory exhaustion (e.g., truncating a 1GB string to 10 characters). The loop should break early once 'n+1' clusters are identified.

unicodedata.combining(ch) only returns the Canonical Combining Class. Many grapheme-extending characters, such as Enclosing Marks (Me) and Spacing Combining Marks (Mc), have a combining class of 0 and will be incorrectly treated as starting a new cluster (e.g., U+20DD Combining Enclosing Circle).
The function fails to handle CRLF (\r\n) as a single grapheme cluster. It will split '\r\n' into two separate clusters, violating UAX #29 and potentially corrupting text rendering.

Hangul Jamo sequences (L, V, T) are not handled. Because Jamo have a combining class of 0, a composed syllable like '가' (U+AC00) represented as Jamo (U+1100 U+1161) will be incorrectly split into multiple clusters.

The ZWJ logic is overly broad; it attaches any following character (including whitespace or control characters) to the previous cluster if it ended with a ZWJ. This doesn't follow the specific Unicode rules for valid emoji ZWJ sequences.

obvious_bugs: O(N) memory/time complexity for small 'n' values
Splitting of CRLF (\r\n) into two characters
Incomplete grapheme boundary detection relying solely on CCC (Combining Class)
notes: This is a typical 'naive' implementation of Unicode truncation. It attempts to handle combining marks and ZWJs but misses several fundamental grapheme cluster rules (CRLF, Hangul, Spacing Marks) and lacks the basic optimization of lazy evaluation/early exit for large strings.
